observation.visible_scene: Top-down view of a white tabletop. Several small pre-formed clusters of shiny metallic magnetic spheres sit stationary on the left and top of the frame. In the center, a person's two hands (gray sweatshirt cuffs) hold a large tangled mass of the same spheres. The right hand begins holding a separate small group of spheres above the mass.
visible_changes: The right hand lowers the small group of spheres from the upper-right toward the top edge of the central mass and brings it into contact, leaving an added protrusion at the top of the mass.
The left hand keeps cradling the main mass on its left side through the early frames, then shifts its grip upward to hold the new top protrusion.
After attaching the small group, the right hand releases, moves out toward the right edge of the frame, and then re-enters to grasp the right side of the mass.

From the middle to the end of the clip both hands hold the mass (left hand on top, right hand on the right), and the mass is rotated and slightly reshaped, shifting its orientation modestly rather than translating across the table.
The stationary table clusters remain in the same positions; the top-middle cluster becomes progressively occluded as the left hand and forearm move upward into that region.
outside_clip_unknowns: How the small group held by the right hand was originally separated from the mass, and what the hands do with the mass after the clip ends.
Whether the added protrusion bonded permanently or was only temporarily placed.
uncertain_details: Exact mechanism of joining (magnetic attraction vs. manual placement) is not visible.
Whether the apparent change in the mass's shape is deformation from pulling or mainly rotation of a rigid cluster.
Camera motion: background clusters stay fixed, suggesting a static top-down camera, but this is inferred from limited evidence.
